metadata.name: Oncology Domain Knowledge Dictionary
metadata.description: Standardized oncology domain vocabulary, variants, abbreviations, and clinical descriptions for Stage 4 SLM prompt engineering and fine-tuning.
metadata.disclaimer: SYNTHETIC RESEARCH USE ONLY — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE

cancer_types.description: The most common type of lung cancer, accounting for approximately 85% of all lung cancer cases.
The most common histological subtype of invasive breast cancer originating in the milk ducts.
Malignancy developing from the epithelial lining of the colon or rectum.
Aggressive skin malignancy arising from melanocytes, strongly driven by MAPK pathway alterations.
Androgen-dependent malignancy of the prostate gland epithelium, graded by Gleason score.
Rare and aggressive adenocarcinoma originating in the intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts.

biomarkers.description: Immune checkpoint surface protein predictive of tumor response to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapies.
Fragmented DNA released by apoptotic or necrotic malignant cells into the peripheral bloodstream, used for minimal residual disease monitoring.
Glycoprotein oncofetal serum marker commonly elevated in colorectal, gastric, and pancreatic carcinomas.
Receptor tyrosine kinase amplified or overexpressed in a subset of breast, gastroesophageal, and ovarian cancers.
Glycoprotein enzyme secreted by prostate epithelial cells; primary serum biomarker for prostate cancer surveillance.
Oncofetal glycoprotein tumor marker utilized in hepatocellular carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, and nonseminomatous germ cell tumors.

mutations.description: Classic sensitizing kinase domain point mutation in exon 21 of EGFR conferring high sensitivity to first-, second-, and third-generation TKIs.
Gatekeeper resistance mutation in EGFR exon 20 mediating resistance to first-generation EGFR inhibitors, targeted by osimertinib.
Valine to glutamic acid substitution at codon 600 constitutively activating the MAPK/ERK pathway in melanoma, colorectal, and thyroid carcinomas.
Common oncogenic GTPase driver alteration in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and colorectal cancer.
Cyclin-dependent kinase alteration associated with genomic tandem duplications and immune gene upregulation in advanced prostate cancers.
Activating mutation in the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway recurrently detected in hepatocellular and biliary tract malignancies.

drugs.description: Humanized monoclonal IgG4 antibody targeting the PD-1 immune checkpoint receptor.
Third-generation oral, CNS-penetrant EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor selective for EGFR-sensitizing and T790M resistance mutations.
Anthracycline topoisomerase II inhibitor cytotoxic antibiotic widely used across hematologic and solid tumor malignancies.
Second-generation platinum antineoplastic alkylating-like agent inducing inter- and intrastrand DNA crosslinks.
Semisynthetic taxane antineoplastic agent that stabilizes tubulin microtubules and inhibits mitotic cell division.
Recombinant humanized monoclonal antibody targeting vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) to inhibit angiogenesis.
Selective, potent adenosine triphosphate-competitive inhibitor of BRAF kinase bearing V600E/K mutations.
Allosteric, non-ATP-competitive small-molecule inhibitor of MEK1 and MEK2 kinases.

drug_combinations.description: Dual MAPK pathway blockade targeting BRAF V600 and MEK1/2 to delay onset of acquired resistance in BRAF-mutant cancers.
Standard doublet cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen combining a platinum cross-linker and taxane microtubule stabilizer.
Chemo-immunotherapy triplet regimen combining anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibition with platinum and taxane cytotoxic backbones.

oncology_abbreviations.description: Standardized 0 to 5 functional assessment scale quantifying a patient's daily activity capability and disease-related functional impairment.
Critical laboratory hematologic measurement calculating the total count of circulating mature and immature neutrophils per microliter.
Clinical surveillance monitoring assessment conducted after therapeutic intervention.
Clinical therapy or pharmacologic intervention administered to manage neoplastic disease.
Time length during and after oncological treatment that a patient lives with disease without progression.
Duration from either diagnosis or start of clinical trial treatment until patient death from any cause.

adverse_events.description: Oncologic emergency defined by absolute neutrophil count < 500 cells/mm3 accompanied by a single temperature spike >= 38.3 C.
Myocardial toxicity or decline in left ventricular ejection fraction triggered by antineoplastic agents like anthracyclines.
Damage to peripheral sensory nerves manifested as numbness, tingling, and paresthesias following taxane or platinum treatment.
Off-target autoimmune inflammation induced by immune checkpoint inhibitors affecting endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, or hepatic tissues.

pathology_terms.description: Histopathologic presence of neoplastic cells within the space surrounding peripheral nerves, associated with increased recurrence.
Presence of malignant tumor cell clusters inside thin-walled lymphatic or blood vascular spaces on histology.
Histopathological identification of tumor cells extending to the inked tissue edge of a resected specimen.

treatment_terms.description: Systemic therapy administered following definitive primary curative surgical resection to eradicate micrometastatic disease.
Systemic treatment delivered before surgical resection to downstage tumor volume and assess in vivo therapeutic response.
Ongoing low-toxicity systemic therapy administered following initial response to prolong disease control and delay progression.

guideline_related_terms.description: Formal diagnostic and treatment process that clinical consensus and evidence determine to be the standard medical practice.
Formal consensus conference of medical oncologists, surgical oncologists, radiation oncologists, radiologists, and molecular pathologists.
